editorial.headline: Land Transport Support Services: Open Nationally, Address-Checked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A national PMA opening applies to towing, transport gas liquefaction, toll collection and truck-cargo surveys, but Bali’s record calls for an address-by-address check.
editorial.body:
KBLI 52219 deals with the service work that sits around land transport rather than the transport movement itself. Its stated scope is practical and specific: towing assistance; gas liquefaction for transport purposes; operation of toll-collection facilities; and surveying of truck cargo. It is a residual grouping for land-transport services not classified elsewhere, which gives it a clear operational character. The point is not a broad transport label, but the defined supporting activities that make a road-based movement possible, measurable, or recoverable when something goes wrong.

Registration is available across the full scale range in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain terms, the classification is not confined to a single enterprise size. What anchors the activity is the service being delivered. An operator using it should be able to recognise its own work in one of the stated functions—towing, gas liquefaction for transport, toll-collection facilities, or truck-cargo surveys—rather than relying only on the broad phrase “related to land transport.” The scope itself supplies the useful perimeter: a defined set of supporting services, not an undifferentiated transport category.

Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%. On those terms, a PMA structure may be fully foreign-owned for this activity at the national level. The listed source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership ceiling in the record: the national position is a full 100% ceiling, stated plainly rather than implied through a general openness label.

Bali needs a separate reading, but the record does not call this activity blocked. It places the activity at medium-high risk and says it is not caught by the moratorium, while asking that the position be verified for the specific address. The provincial moratorium is described as permanent and island-wide for PMA activities at Low and Medium-Low risk. Accordingly, foreign PMA registration for this activity is not barred by that moratorium in Bali. A national 100% ceiling is real, but in Bali the proposed address still needs checking. The record supplies no separate Bali foreign-ownership percentage; its Bali qualification is the risk-based, address-specific one.
